statement.p: A rope, attached to a weight, goes up through a pulley at the ceiling and back down to a worker. The worker holds the rope at the same height as the connection point between the rope and weight. The distance from the connection point to the ceiling is 30 ft. Suppose the worker stands directly next to the weight (i.e., a total rope length of 60 ft) and begins to walk away at a constant rate of 3 ft/s. How fast is the weight rising when the worker has walked:

static.solution:
Solution:
The worker, weight and pulley form a right triangle with height 30, base length x, and hypotenuse z. The speed at which the weight rises is the same as the speed the rope is being pulled. This means the rate we are looking for is \dfrac{dz}{dt}.
By the Pythagorean Theorem, x^2 + 30^2 = z^2 Take time-derivatives of both sides of the equation. 2x\dfrac{dx}{dt} = 2z\dfrac{dz}{dt}.
Then plug in \dfrac{dx}{dt} = 3 and solve for the unknown rate. \dfrac{dz}{dt} = \dfrac{3 x}{z}.
When x = 10, 10^2 + 30^2 = z^2 \;\Rightarrow\; z = \sqrt{1000}. \Rightarrow \dfrac{dz}{dt} = \dfrac{30}{\sqrt{1000}} \approx 0.948683298050514.
When x = 30, 30^2 + 30^2 = z^2 \;\Rightarrow\; z = \sqrt{1800}. \Rightarrow \dfrac{dz}{dt} = \dfrac{90}{\sqrt{1800}} \approx 2.12132034355964.
